'''Helmut Grunsky''' (11 July 1904 – 5 June 1986) was a German mathematician who worked in [[complex analysis]] and [[geometric function theory]]. He introduced [[Grunsky's theorem]] and the [[Grunsky inequalities]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Jenkins|1989}}</ref>

In 1936, he was appointed editor of ''[[Jahrbuch über die Fortschritte der Mathematik]]''. In 1939 he was forced to leave this position after [[Ludwig Bieberbach]] accused him of employing Jewish referees in a notorious letter.<ref>{{harvtxt|Siegmund-Schultze|2004}}</ref> He joined the [[Nazi Party]] on 1 April 1940, though he seems to have had little sympathy with its philosophy.<ref>{{cite book |last=Siegmund-Schultze |first=Reinhard |title=Mathematicians Fleeing from Nazi Germany: Individual Fates and Global Impact |page=25|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jBoEmGB3B3MC&dq=Helmut+grunsky+NSDAP&pg=PA25 |date=2009|publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=9780691140414|access-date=26 March 2022}}</ref> He published in the journal [[Deutsche Mathematik]]. From 1949 he was Privatdozent at the [[University of Tübingen]]; later, he was professor at the [[University of Mainz]] and at the [[University of Würzburg]].
